chunks: From him, he said: Dawud ibn Ishaq Abu Suleyman al-Hazza’ narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Fayz from Taym al-Ribaab, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

'I dislike the man if I see in his leg a sandal that is not narrowed (at the instep). Indeed, the first one to change the shoe-style of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was So-and-so.' Then he said: 'What do you call this shoe-style?' I said: 'Al-Mamsouh.' He said: 'This is Al-Mamsouh.'

key_terms.الْمَمْسُوحَ: Al-Mamsouh (a specific type of sandal with a strap across the instep, often associated with the change from the Prophet's style)
key_terms.مُخَصَّرَةٍ: Narrowed at the instep (a specific style of sandal)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'Mamsouh' sandal style in Shia jurisprudence and how does it differ from the Prophet's footwear?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the 'Mamsouh' style—characterized by a lack of narrowing at the instep—as the specific deviation from the Prophet’s (PBUH) footwear, linking this sartorial change to the era of the Umayyads, particularly Caliph Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz or his predecessors, as a marker of shifting social customs. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *Tashabbuh* (imitation) and the preservation of distinct Prophetic identity through even minor details of dress, serving as a practical guide for distinguishing authentic Sunnah from later cultural innovations.
